transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-03
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (OmniLytics Head of ML), Daniel Cho (Platform), Priya Patel (Data Scientist)
Shared: Benchmark spreadsheet (live): https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/omnilytics-aug2025, Security docs: /sec/soc2, Screen: Marcus - results dashboard

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): quick review of latest benchmark runs vs customer's baseline provider, discussed latency and throughput tradeoffs, identified tuning steps (batching, KV prefix cache, quant), agreed next runs and deliverables.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll give it a minute for folks to pop in. this is the weekly POC sync for OmniLytics, benchmark review vs the baseline provider. agenda - quick recap, run through numbers from last night, proposed tuning, next steps.
[00:23] Sofia Ramirez: thanks Alicia. we got the invite. excited to see numbers.
[00:28] Daniel Cho: morning. short on time but we'll hang for the key parts.
[00:35] Marcus Li: hi all, Marcus from Redwood infra, I'll share my screen in a sec; quick note, some timestamps in the spreadsheet are PST but the runner nodes were us-west2 region.
[00:46] Priya Patel: good to know, thanks.
[01:02] Alicia Park: okay Marcus, take it away.
[01:06] Marcus Li: yep. so slide 1 of the dashboard - run summary: we compared 3 configs: baseline provider (their managed endpoint), Redwood Hosted default (rdefault small pool), and Redwood Dedicated quantized variant (int8-ish - note: not perfect int8, we used q4-ish). the test harness used 1000 requests over 10 minutes with arrival pattern that mimics bursty traffic; payload average token length 120 tokens.
[01:38] Marcus Li: baseline provider 95th latency was 420 ms, p50 around 120 ms, throughput ~180 rps sustained. Redwood Hosted default 95th latency 320 ms, p50 95 ms, throughput 220 rps. Redwood Dedicated quantized 95th latency 180 ms, p50 60 ms, throughput 520 rps. those are the headline numbers.
[02:05] Sofia Ramirez: wait so dedicated is 2-3x faster at throughput vs baseline? that's big. Are you sure the workloads are apples-to-apples?
[02:18] Marcus Li: good question. we tried to match model weights (same open model variant you requested), same prompt sets, same concurrency distribution. differences: baseline provider had smaller batch window and lower autoscale headroom, also encrypted network hop to their region. Redwood dedicated used local GPU pool with optimized kernels + micro-batching and prefix KV cache retained between calls for re-use.
[02:44] Priya Patel: can you clarify the caching - was the KV cache warmed for these tests?
[02:51] Marcus Li: yes warmed for 30% of prefixes. we have metrics in sheet: cache hit rate ~26% which reduced token generation work for repeated conversation patterns. baseline provider does not support persistent KV across requests in their managed endpoint per our notes.
[03:08] Daniel Cho: hmm that could be biasing throughput. can we see a run without cache?
[03:12] Marcus Li: absolutely - we included a no-cache run. no-cache dedicated 95th latency 260 ms, p50 90 ms, throughput 330 rps. so still better than baseline but gap reduces.
[03:26] Alicia Park: this is expected; caching helps but even without it the dedicated pool and optimized kernels still win due to lower queuing and GPU utilization patterns.
[03:34] Sofia Ramirez: pricing - what about cost per 1M tokens? baseline is cheaper nominally for hosted - we need cost delta.
[03:40] Alicia Park: we'll attach a cost comparison in the updated sheet. short answer: hosted baseline lower per-token for small scale but at scale the dedicated unit economics with higher throughput reduces cost per effective request. Marcus will add per-token compute and amortized infra numbers.
[03:58] Marcus Li: added note - quantization profile important: q4_0 preserved quality for your eval set; q8 gave better perf but introduced a small quality regression on rare tokens. we ran rouge-like similarity and a human eval sample - drop was within your tolerance except in named-entity heavy prompts.
[04:20] Priya Patel: that matches what we saw earlier. named entities are sensitive. can we run targeted eval with our NER set?
[04:27] Marcus Li: yes, please share the NER sample and we'll run the targeted eval.
[04:31] Sofia Ramirez: action: we'll share NER sample by Friday.
[04:36] Alicia Park: noted.
[04:44] Marcus Li: moving on to latency tail analysis - here's a waterfall. (screen) baseline provider shows a long network hop at ~75 ms median added; plus queueing spikes at concurrency > 200. Redwood dedicated queueing kicks in around 700 concurrent requests.
[05:04] Marcus Li: we also instrumented kernel-level metrics - attention kernel stalls were low on our optimized runtime. GPU util was 85% sustained for dedicated run, 62% for baseline.
[05:18] Daniel Cho: 85% is good. which GPU family was used for dedicated?
[05:22] Marcus Li: A100-80GB equivalent V2s. baseline provider was running on mixed A100 and older V100s per their public doc.
[05:30] Sofia Ramirez: can we lock to specific GPU types in the dedicated offer?
[05:33] Alicia Park: yes, Dedicated lets you pin pool type; we'll include an option with A100-only pool and price delta in the sheet.
[05:40] Priya Patel: latency jitter - what's the 99th?
[05:44] Marcus Li: baseline 99th ~950 ms, Redwood Hosted ~720 ms, Dedicated quantized ~420 ms (with cache), no-cache dedicated ~640 ms.
[06:00] Sofia Ramirez: okay that 99th difference matters for our user SLO (95th < 500ms). seems dedicated quantized meets it with cache, no-cache borderline.
[06:12] Alicia Park: correct. next steps include either ensure caching patterns or tune batching thresholds to reduce the no-cache tail. Marcus had two experimental knobs he wanted to try? Marcus?
[06:23] Marcus Li: yes, two knobs: 1) adaptive batch window increase for mid-concurrency bursts (adds ~20-40ms p50 but reduces 95th by 15-25%), 2) larger KV shard retention to increase cache hit rate (might increase memory footprint). we propose running A/B of these for next run.
[06:42] Priya Patel: memory footprint concerns are fine for us on dedicated. we can increase.
[06:46] Daniel Cho: from infra side we need to check quotas but likely ok.
[06:50] Alicia Park: great.
[06:54] Marcus Li: also a note on model variants: there's a slimmed variant that trims embeddings for faster decode - we'll test that. quality tradeoffs may show up on entity prompts.
[07:06] Sofia Ramirez: can you annotate which runs used which model variant in the spreadsheet? sometimes the naming got swapped in earlier runs.
[07:12] Marcus Li: will do, I'll add a variant column and tag run ids.
[07:18] Alicia Park: moving to security/compliance; OmniLytics asked about audit logs and KMS. we validated Redwood supports customer-managed KMS, per-run audit logs, and SOC 2 doc is attached. any open questions?
[07:31] Sofia Ramirez: we need encryption-at-rest verification and retention policy for logs - 90 days okay? we also want to see sample audit log entry format.
[07:40] Marcus Li: we will share sample audit log json and confirm retention config - 90 days is supported in our enterprise package; can be extended.
[07:48] Daniel Cho: also SSO/SAML - does Redwood support SCIM provisioning?
[07:52] Alicia Park: yes SSO SAML and SCIM supported. we'll include the guide link.
[07:58] Priya Patel: ok thanks.
[08:05] Marcus Li: jumping back to numbers - I want to call out one outlier run where p95 spiked to 1.2s on dedicated. root cause looked like an autoscaler lag due to a vertical compaction job running on the node; we flagged that and re-ran. it's in the raw logs.
[08:20] Priya Patel: good you re-ran. can you share both raw logs and cleaned summary?
[08:26] Marcus Li: yes both in the shared folder.
[08:29] Alicia Park: any questions on the baseline comparison methodology?
[08:33] Sofia Ramirez: one more - baseline provider uses regional failover which adds variability; did you simulate regional outage?
[08:40] Marcus Li: not in these runs. we can run a chaos run to emulate a failover. that will show our routing fallback behavior vs their multi-region setup.
[08:48] Daniel Cho: add that to next runs, please.
[08:51] Alicia Park: will do.
[08:54] Marcus Li: quick note on metrics: we captured p50/p95/p99, GPU util, queue depth, batch sizes, cache hits, and per-request cost estimate. the sheet has per-run cost estimate to compute only. not included network egress and other infra.
[09:10] Priya Patel: can we get end-to-end cost (including egress)?
[09:12] Alicia Park: yes we'll approximate egress for your region; Marcus will add that.
[09:18] Marcus Li: also added a sensitivity analysis - if token length increases to 300 tokens, dedicated throughput drops 30% but still outperforms baseline on cost at scale. details in sheet.
[09:30] Sofia Ramirez: ok useful.
[09:35] Alicia Park: last piece - timeline for pilot extension and go/no-go criteria. Sofia, you mentioned you want a week of sustained 95th < 500ms and cost within 1.5x baseline to move to a pilot extension? is that right?
[09:46] Sofia Ramirez: roughly yes. also need security sign-off and a small production shadow run with write-protect.
[09:52] Alicia Park: noted. we'll aim to get the runs and docs in the next two weeks.
[09:56] Marcus Li: proposed A/B runs: A) caching + adaptive batching, B) no cache + higher batch cap. we'll run each for 30 minutes with the same adversarial traffic pattern.
[10:06] Daniel Cho: how long to schedule?
[10:08] Marcus Li: about 2-3 hours to spin up and warm cache; the runs themselves 30 minutes each. plus log collection. so ask for a maintenance window; Alicia we'll coordinate.
[10:17] Alicia Park: I'll coordinate with Sofia for timing.
[10:20] Priya Patel: question - can we do the targeted NER eval on quantized q4 variant only? we want to keep cost low.
[10:26] Marcus Li: yes q4 targeted eval will be done. we'll include the human-eval csv.
[10:31] Sofia Ramirez: any blockers from Redwood side on giving us access to dedicated pool for benchmarking?
[10:35] Alicia Park: no blockers; we'll provision a sandbox dedicated pool under the POC account. it'll have a short TTL. pricing will be in the sheet.
[10:43] Daniel Cho: please include the exact instance/GPU SKU and the node counts.
[10:47] Marcus Li: will add.
[10:50] Alicia Park: okay quick recap of action items and next steps.
[10:53] Marcus Li: action items - I'll run the A/B runs, upload logs, and tag run ids in the spreadsheet.
[10:57] Alicia Park: I'll send updated spreadsheet with annotated runs, cost breakdown, and SOC2 excerpt by Friday (2025-09-05).
[11:02] Sofia Ramirez: OmniLytics will share NER test sample and production trace sample by 2025-09-05.
[11:07] Priya Patel: and we'll confirm internal quotas by 2025-09-08.
[11:10] Alicia Park: great. any last Qs?
[11:13] Daniel Cho: none from me.
[11:15] Sofia Ramirez: no, thanks everyone.
[11:18] Alicia Park: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
[11:21] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-recognitions (q4_0 vs q4o). referenced artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet link, sample audit log (will be shared), and a short human eval csv.
